column1: # The fork-isolation scenario, driven by `just test-fork <arch>`.
# `/bin/forktest` fills two separately aligned 4 KiB writable pages, forks, and checks both
# directions of the copy. The child writes one page and verifies its own write, and the parent
# verifies that write did not land in its view. Then the parent writes the other page while the
# child only ever *reads* it, and the child checks that page still holds its fork-time contents
# after a wait long enough for the parent's write to have happened.
# That second direction is the one this gate exists for: a page the child writes gets a private
# copy either way, so only a read of a page the child never wrote shows a fork whose frames are
# shared rather than copied (`KNOWN_ISSUES.md` item 27, in the direction nobody had tested).
# The expected line is the last one the program prints, and it is printed only after the parent
# has waited for the child and checked its exit status - so a child that failed a phase, or one
# that hung, cannot produce it. A hung child leaves the parent in `waitpid` and the step
# unanswered, which the harness reports as this step not answering.
# One step and not four, because the four lines come from one run and a step asserts one whole
# line. The lines before this one are diagnostics for the failure, not separate claims. The
# expectation is not a prefix of the command: the command is `/bin/forktest`, every line starts
# `forktest: `.
# The child's spin is what makes the sharing *visible* rather than what makes this pass: the
# child reads its own private copy either way, so the check cannot fail spuriously - a run that
# passes is a pass, and the spin only bounds how early a broken fork could hide. That is why
# this gate can sit in `test-arches` without being a flake risk.
/bin/forktest
